chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr al-Khasha'i, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and sat near him, and behold, Najjah had asked permission and was granted entry. He entered and knelt on his knees, then said, 'I am your ransom, I wish to ask you a question, and by God I do not intend by it except the freeing of my neck from the Fire.' He seemed to be moved by him, sat up straight, and said to him, 'O Najjah, ask me, and I will not leave you without informing you of anything you ask me today.' He said, 'I am your ransom, what do you say about so-and-so and so-and-so?' He said, 'O Najjah, we have the khums in the Book of God, and we have the anfal, and we have the choicest of wealth. And they, by God, were the first to wrong us, and they established our right in the Book of God, and the first to make people carry us on their necks, and our blood is in their throats until the Day of Judgment due to our wronging the People of the House. And indeed, people are revolving in the forbidden until the Day of Judgment due to our wronging the People of the House.' Najjah said, 'To God we belong and to Him we shall return,' three times, 'We are ruined, by the Lord of the Ka'ba.'

He lifted his thigh from the cushion, faced the qibla, and made a supplication of which I understood nothing, except that we heard him at the end of his supplication saying, 'O God, we have made that permissible for our shi'a.' He then turned his face to us and said, 'O Najjah, upon the fitrah of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) are none but us and our shi'a.'

If a questioner says, 'All that you have mentioned only indicates permission for you to manage these lands, and does not indicate that it is valid for you to own them through purchase and sale,' then if purchase and sale are not valid, what is a branch of them that is also not valid, such as waqf, nihla, hibah, and what runs in their manner? It was said to him, 'We have divided the lands in the past into three categories: A land whose people surrender it, so it is left in their hands and it is their property; thus, for us, the ruling of this is valid, and our purchase and sale of it are valid. As for the lands that are taken by conquest or whose people make peace with us upon it, we have been permitted their purchase and sale because we have a share in that, because they are lands of the Muslims, and in this category also, purchase and sale are valid in this manner. As for the anfal and what runs in their manner, ownership through purchase and sale is not valid for us, and we are only permitted management as needed. And that which indicates the second category is what has been narrated.'
Book: Tahdhib al-Ahkam, Chapter: 39 - The Chapter of Additions, Hadith number: 24
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on the Imam's ownership and management of land and wealth according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the Ahl al-Bayt's exclusive right to *khums* and *anfal*, framing the world's wealth as a consequence of the injustice done to them. It provides a nuanced juristic classification of land ownership, distinguishing between private property, conquered lands, and *anfal*, thereby validating specific modes of transaction like purchase and sale for certain categories while reserving direct management for others. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for understanding the economic authority of the Imams and the practical application of divine wealth distribution.
